title: Corrosion Inspection of the Cabin Seat Track Splice Joints
abstract: Corrosion inspection of the cabin seat track splice joints between stations 41 and 48, with the blend-out limits and the reporting rule for a joint next to a galley or lavatory.

sections.purpose: This task gives the corrosion inspection of the seat track splice joints between stations 41 and 48, which are the joints most exposed to galley and lavatory spillage.
sections.job_setup_note: Seats and floor panels must be out over the full length of the inspected bays. Clean the splice area before the visual inspection: dried spillage residue looks very like light pitting and gives false findings. The blend-out limits in the illustration are the maximum for this task; anything beyond them is an engineering assessment and not a line finding. Record the joint position of every finding, because the trend across the fleet is tracked by joint position.
sections.procedure: 1. Remove the cabin seats and the floor panels between stations 41 and 48 in zones 241 and 251. 2. Clean the splice joints and remove all spillage residue. 3. Do a detailed visual inspection of each splice strap D5350129600648 and of the forward lug D5350123241140. 4. Do a detailed visual inspection of the seat track flange under each strap. 5. Give particular attention to the joints next to the mid galley and the mid lavatory. 6. Where corrosion is found, remove the strap and clean the faying surface to bare metal. CAUTION: DO NOT USE A STEEL WIRE BRUSH ON THE SEAT TRACK. STEEL PARTICLES LEFT IN THE ALUMINIUM SURFACE START A NEW CORROSION CELL. 7. Measure the corrosion depth with the depth gauge and compare it with the limits in the illustration. 8. Blend out corrosion that is inside the limits and restore the protective treatment. WARNING: DO NOT BLEND OUT CORROSION THAT IS DEEPER THAN THE LIMIT IN THE ILLUSTRATION. THE SEAT TRACK LOAD PATH CAN BE COMPROMISED AND AN ENGINEERING ASSESSMENT IS REQUIRED. 9. Install the strap wet with sealant and torque the joint. 10. Renew the clevis pins LN666073-13 and the cushioned clamps EN220364-30 in every disturbed bay. 11. Install the floor panels and the seats.
sections.close_out: Record every finding by joint position, with the measured depth and the action taken, on the aircraft work card. Do a seat track locking check before the aircraft returns to service. Report any joint that has now been blended twice, because a second blend usually means the strap has to be replaced at the next visit.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. Six-year interval, counted from delivery or from the last accomplishment of this task.

safety_precautions: Make sure that the cabin floor is supported where panels are removed.
Do not use a steel wire brush on aluminium structure.
Obey the sealant handling precautions in the standard practice.

title: Corrosion Inspection of the Cabin Seat Track Splice Joints

issue.reason: Embodiment of the corrosion-resistant strap standard written in as an optional continuation of the inspection, and the inspection itself withdrawn on aircraft that take it.

abstract: Corrosion inspection of the cabin seat track splice joints between stations 41 and 48, with the blend-out limits, the reporting rule for a joint next to a galley or lavatory, and the strap change that can be embodied from the same access.

sections.purpose: This task gives the corrosion inspection of the seat track splice joints between stations 41 and 48, which are the joints most exposed to galley and lavatory spillage.
sections.job_setup_note: Seats and floor panels must be out over the full length of the inspected bays. Decide before the visit whether the corrosion-resistant strap standard is to be embodied at the same time: the access is identical and the decision cannot sensibly be taken once the floor is closed again. Clean the splice area before the visual inspection: dried spillage residue looks very like light pitting and gives false findings. The blend-out limits in the illustration are the maximum for this task; anything beyond them is an engineering assessment and not a line finding. Record the joint position of every finding, because the trend across the fleet is tracked by joint position.
sections.procedure: 1. Remove the cabin seats and the floor panels between stations 41 and 48 in zones 241 and 251. 2. Clean the splice joints and remove all spillage residue. 3. Do a detailed visual inspection of each splice strap D5350129600648 and of the forward lug D5350123241140. 4. Do a detailed visual inspection of the seat track flange under each strap. 5. Give particular attention to the joints next to the mid galley and the mid lavatory. 6. Where corrosion is found, remove the strap and clean the faying surface to bare metal. CAUTION: DO NOT USE A STEEL WIRE BRUSH ON THE SEAT TRACK. STEEL PARTICLES LEFT IN THE ALUMINIUM SURFACE START A NEW CORROSION CELL. 7. Measure the corrosion depth with the depth gauge and compare it with the limits in the illustration. 8. Blend out corrosion that is inside the limits and restore the protective treatment. WARNING: DO NOT BLEND OUT CORROSION THAT IS DEEPER THAN THE LIMIT IN THE ILLUSTRATION. THE SEAT TRACK LOAD PATH CAN BE COMPROMISED AND AN ENGINEERING ASSESSMENT IS REQUIRED. 9. Where MOD-161330 is to be embodied at this visit, do not refit the removed straps: fit the corrosion-resistant straps of the modification instead, re-shim the forward lug to take up the thickness difference and continue at step 10. Every joint between stations 41 and 48 must be converted; a part-converted cabin is not a configuration. 10. Install the strap wet with sealant and torque the joint. 11. Renew the clevis pins LN666073-13 and the cushioned clamps EN220364-30 in every disturbed bay. 12. Install the floor panels and the seats.
sections.close_out: Record every finding by joint position, with the measured depth and the action taken, on the aircraft work card. Where the strap standard was converted at this visit, record the embodiment against MOD-161330 and remove this task from the aircraft maintenance programme; it does not apply to the converted configuration. Do a seat track locking check before the aircraft returns to service. Report any joint that has now been blended twice, because a second blend usually means the strap has to be replaced at the next visit.

type_data.effectivity_note: Pre MOD-161330 aircraft: six-year interval. Post MOD-161330 aircraft: this task is withdrawn. The corrosion-resistant strap is installed wet at every faying surface and the mid cabin floor is covered by the twelve-year structural check instead, so repeating this inspection on a converted aircraft opens the floor for nothing.

safety_precautions: Make sure that the cabin floor is supported where panels are removed.
Do not use a steel wire brush on aluminium structure.
Obey the sealant handling precautions in the standard practice.
